brief.headline: Lindy has new evening confusion (including a stove left on), a 7.5% weight loss since Sep 5, and low mood with missed day center days. She started apixaban on Sep 8.

items.statement: On 2026-11-11 the RN documented about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Lindy was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The plan was urinalysis, medication review, and a PCP visit that week. The notes provided show no urinalysis result or confusion work-up outcome.
items.verifier_note: The 11-11 RN note matches every detail: two weeks of evening confusion, the stove left on once, oriented to person and place but not date, no fever, and the plan. The note has no urinalysis result, so the absence claim holds.

items.statement: Weight fell at every reading, from 86.6 kg on 2026-09-05 to 84.3 kg on 10-01, 82.1 kg on 10-28 and 80.1 kg on 11-24. That is 6.5 kg (14.3 lb, 7.5%) over about 11 weeks. The dietitian notes poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan is a nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record shows weight falling at each of the four readings. It gives -6.5 kg, -14.3 lb and -7.5%. The dietitian note supports the poor appetite, skipped breakfast, 50% of lunches, and the plan. Sep 5 to Nov 24 is about 11 weeks.

items.statement: Lindy missed 4 of 8 scheduled day center days as of 2026-11-15. When present she was quiet and left activities early. On 11-17 she told the social worker she feels "down" and does not want to leave the house since a close friend died last month. A depression screen and grief support are planned. She attended on 11-18, joined chair exercise and music group, and ate most of lunch.
items.verifier_note: Notes n002, n003 and n010 support the missed days, the quiet behavior and early departures, the "down" mood and the friend's death last month. They also support the planned depression screen and grief support, and the 11-18 attendance, activities and lunch.

items.statement: Apixaban 5 mg was started on 2026-09-08 for new atrial fibrillation found on ECG. The pharmacist reconciled it on 09-10 and updated the blister pack. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks, and no recheck is documented in the notes provided. Clopidogrel remains on the active list.
items.verifier_note: The start date, indication, pharmacist reconciliation and blister pack update, and the 4-week recheck plan are supported. No cited source mentions clopidogrel or says it remains on the active list. The medication record lists only apixaban as started and nothing as stopped.

questions_for_team: Has the urinalysis and medication review from 11-11 been completed, and what were the results? The PCP note of 11-13 does not mention the confusion.
Does the home safety risk (stove left on) need a plan, such as a home safety check or added supervision?
Could mood, grief, appetite or dental problems explain both the weight loss and the withdrawal? When will the depression screen be done?
Was the 4-week apixaban recheck completed? Should the new medication be considered in the confusion review?
Is the current nutrition plan enough given the steady weight decline, and who will track the weekly weights?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions/discharges in that window, including reasons and discharge instructions.

Review the new atrial fibrillation finding: date first identified on ECG, who diagnosed it, whether rate/rhythm plan and anticoagulation follow-up (apixaban started 2026-09-08) are documented, and whether any bleeding events, bruising, or dose/renal-function checks are recorded.

Medication reconciliation: confirm apixaban start is on the active list with dose and adherence; review concurrent clopidogrel plus apixaban for bleeding-risk discussion flagged for prescriber review; check metoprolol, simvastatin, and nitroglycerin spray for changes, refills, or missed doses; note any new starts or stops since last review.

Heart failure monitoring (chronic CHF, onset 2024): daily or weekly weight trend with flagged gains, edema, dyspnea, orthopnea, diuretic status (none appears on active list, so confirm whether one was stopped or never prescribed), potassium/renal labs, and any BNP or echo follow-up.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window, including orthostatic readings and any resting HR values relevant to beta-blocker dosing and new AF.
Falls and fall-risk review: any falls, near-falls, or fall-related injuries, especially with anticoagulation now started; gait/balance and assistive device use.

Bleeding and anemia review: history of anemia (onset 1987), recent hemoglobin/CBC values, melena, hematuria, epistaxis, or bruising since apixaban start; check whether labs were ordered for monitoring.

Respiratory status for emphysema: rescue inhaler use, oxygen use if any, SpO2 readings, exacerbations, steroid or antibiotic courses, and pulmonary rehab or vaccination status. Note that no inhaler appears on the active medication list, so verify whether one is missing from the list.
Glycemic and metabolic review for prediabetes and obesity: most recent A1c or glucose values, BMI trend, dietary or activity counseling, and whether a lab recheck is due.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, meal preparation, medication management, and transportation; compare to the prior review baseline.

Cognition, mood, and attendance: any new cognitive concerns, depression screen scores, social isolation, missed IDT or day-program attendance, and whether a caregiver or support person is still in place, including any caregiver strain or changes in living situation.

Care-plan items due: list any goals, screenings, advance directive or code status check, caregiver assessment, and follow-up appointments with due dates in or near the window; flag overdue items for the team.

Summarize all changes since last review (new diagnoses, med starts/stops, ED visits, weight and BP shifts, functional decline) as discussion items for the IDT, without recommending specific treatment changes; leave decisions to the clinicians.
